item.title: Kerry Association in New York names Dr Elizabeth Stack as Person of the Year
item.description: The Kerry Association in New York has announced Dr Elizabeth Stack as its 2026 Kerry Person of the Year. Dr Stack is a distinguished historian, educator, and museum leader, originally from Listowel, who is currently the Education Director at the Celtic Junction Arts Centre in Minnesota. Dr Stack has been announced as the Kerry Person of the Year in recognition of her outstanding contributions to Irish and Irish/American history, culture, and community life. item.title: Over €65 million in funding announced for roads in Kerry
item.description: Over €65 million in funding has been announced for roads in Kerry. It’s part of a national €1.5 billion package announced today by Transport Minister, Darragh O’Brien and Transport Infrastructure Ireland. It includes funding for projects including the development of the Farranfore to Killarney bypass, and works on the Dingle-Tralee road and the N70 in South Kerry. item.title: England name 15 to take on Ireland on Saturday
item.description: Henry Pollock will earn a first start for England in their Six Nations clash with Ireland at Twickenham on Saturday. The Northampton Saints youngster has been named in the back row in his eighth international appearance. Captain Maro Itoje earns his 100th cap in the second-row, Advertisement While Henry Arundell starts on the wing, having been cleared to play by a disciplinary committee earlier.

item.title: FAI Chief to address Israel games 'soon'
item.description: Carla Ward has revealed that FAI chief executive David Courell will address the media 'soon' in relation to the Men's Nations League. The Ireland senior women's head coach was asked about the contentious games against Israel. The FAI have not spoken to the media since last week's draw. Advertisement

item.title: New deal for Saka at Arsenal
item.description: Arsenal have secured the services of winger Bukayo Saka until at least 2031. The England star has signed a new five-year deal with the Gunners, and is now the club's best-paid player, earning upwards of 340-thousand euro a week. Saka has scored seven goals in 33 appearances for the club across all competitions this season. Advertisement

item.title: Heavy rains finishes Ireland's World Cup hopes
item.description: Heavy rain has finished off the chances of both Ireland and Australia at the T-20 World Cup. Ireland's fourth group match against Zimbabwe had to be abandoned without a ball being bowled. It means that Zimbabwe advance to the Super Eights, with Australia and Ireland getting eliminated by virtue of points being shared in Pallekele. Advertisement
